lines: Kiln is an open-source office suite that opens, edits and saves real Microsoft Office files and feels
immediately familiar to Office users, while looking and feeling like its own product: warmer, calmer and
faster, with features Office lacks such as a command palette with Office synonyms, built-in version
history, self-hosted live collaboration and presenter view everywhere.
Pagination and line breaking are deterministic code using bundled font metrics, so a long
document paginates identically on every platform and identically in the exported PDF. The
layout engine owns the hot loop of layout, invalidation, culling and glyph caching, and the
painter only blits tiles and glyph quads onto the canvas of each page.
Fidelity is measured, not claimed: every
fixture in the corpus is opened, laid out and
compared with a reference rendering, and a
regression in the number of lines of any
paragraph fails the build before it reaches
anyone who depends on their documents
looking the way they wrote them.
